ui.disclaimer: An invented coordination exercise, not an epidemiological forecast or medical advice. All local people, reports, quantities, trade-offs and outcomes are fictional.
ui.intro: You coordinate one night of deliveries, staff planning and public communication. Inspect three reports, pack a limited shipment and leave an honest handover. No time limit.
ui.inspect: Read all three reports before dispatch. Tap a location or its button. Drag to orbit; pinch to zoom.
ui.allocation: Assign all six crates. Requests total nine. These are fictional logistics tokens, not medical supply calculations. You can revise until sealing.
ui.fallback: 3D is unavailable on this device. The complete decision exercise remains playable below.
ui.noForecast: No infections, deaths or probabilities are predicted. Outcomes describe only this invented handover.
ui.bridgePlan: Exercise assumption: the bridge plan is 3 hospital, 2 clinic and 1 outreach crate. These invented targets are not clinical ratios.
ui.sceneHint: Drag to look · scroll to zoom

0.speaker: Historical context
0.text: WHO characterized COVID-19 as a pandemic on 11 March 2020. On 30 March it called for maintaining essential health services alongside the response.

1.speaker: Fictional shift · 18:00
1.text: Rain beads on the loading-bay windows. A hospital, a small clinic and residents without transport are waiting. You are the district coordinator, not a clinician. Tonight, make the gaps visible.

reports.prompt: Inspect the reports before making promises.

ward.label: Hospital desk
ward.title: A bed is not a staffed service
ward.description: Fictional report: the hospital requests four crates. Staff are stretched, and a room without trained staff is not extra service capacity. The night lead asks you to protect a staffed roster, not promise a bed count.

ledger.label: Clinic ledger
ledger.title: Care beyond the outbreak
ledger.description: Fictional report: the clinic requests three crates to support essential services. Diverting every worker to one response would leave its existing appointments without a plan. The ledger records unmet needs, not case forecasts.

radio.label: Community radio
radio.title: Who cannot reach the queue?
radio.description: Fictional report: volunteers request two crates for residents without transport. Online announcements miss some households. A rumor says every delivery is guaranteed. No one has verified the next truck’s arrival.

0.speaker: Fictional shift · 20:00
0.text: The manifest is sealed. Every crate sent somewhere is a crate unavailable elsewhere. The clinic calls again: tomorrow’s roster is still blank.

roster.title: 21:00 · Service continuity
roster.prompt: How will you plan the next shift?

continuity.label: Protect essential-service staff
continuity.description: Keep a named clinic roster and request additional support. The hospital does not get every available worker tonight.

surge.label: Concentrate the available team
surge.description: Move the planning team toward the hospital. The clinic’s continuity plan is deferred; record that gap rather than claiming extra staffed beds.

transparent.label: Publish what is known and unknown
transparent.description: Share the actual manifest, the unfilled requests and a next update time. Use radio and translated print notices as well as online channels.

certainty.label: Promise that all requests will be met
certainty.description: A reassuring headline, but the next truck is unconfirmed. You will need to face the mismatch between the promise and the manifest.

briefing.title: 22:00 · The public briefing
briefing.prompt: The microphone is live. What can you honestly promise?

correct.label: Correct the promise publicly
correct.description: Name the mistake, publish the gaps and set a new update time. The correction is useful, but does not erase the earlier promise.

silent.label: Leave the headline unchanged
silent.description: Avoid a difficult correction tonight. Residents still have a guarantee that the dispatch record cannot support.

correction.title: 23:00 · A caller challenges the promise
correction.prompt: “Our request is missing from the manifest.” Your earlier assurance is now part of the problem.

0.speaker: Fictional shift · 00:00
0.text: The next coordinator opens your notebook. It cannot tell them how many people will fall ill. It can tell them who was supplied, which services still need a plan and whether the public heard the same truth.

manifest.prompt: Assign all six crates. Requests total nine. These are fictional logistics tokens, not medical supply calculations. You can revise until sealing.

shared.title: An accountable handover
shared.subtitle: No perfect allocation. No hidden gaps.

0.text: In this fictional outcome, all three destinations receive support, essential-service planning survives and the public record acknowledges uncertainty. Unfilled requests remain. This is a workable handover, not a claim that the outbreak was controlled.

In this fictional outcome, an uncorrected guarantee conflicts with limited supplies. The next coordinator inherits a communication problem as well as unmet requests. No illness or mortality outcome is implied.

gap.title: A district left uneven
gap.subtitle: Someone is missing from the plan.

0.text: In this fictional outcome, at least one destination gets no crates or essential-service planning is deferred. The handover must name these gaps. A full hospital loading bay is not the same as a supported district.

partial.title: A repairable plan
partial.subtitle: An honest record of difficult trade-offs.

0.text: In this fictional outcome, the record preserves some useful decisions but the allocation falls short of the exercise’s balanced plan. Review the requests, not a score. A new shift lets you compare a different handover without pretending to predict a pandemic.
